item.title: Building Vacancy Detection With GeoAI Using Proxy Data in a Constrained and Mixed Access Environment
item.description: Transactions in GIS, Volume 30, Issue 7, November 2026.
item.dc:description: ABSTRACT This article presents a GeoAI model designed to predict building vacancy in Ireland using only open and licensed‐but‐accessible datasets. It operates under mixed‐access, proxy‐based conditions, as legal and technical barriers frequently restrict access to proprietary data like utility consumption. Our model achieved a 0.379 F1‐score and 0.348 F1‐score under temporal holdout conditions, establishing a new baseline, with performance proving stronger in urban areas compared to rural regions. These results suggest limitations when relying solely on the available proxy data, highlighting the difficulty of detecting vacancy in environments where utility data are not readily available. This study prioritizes a schema‐agnostic, reproducible architecture and governance framework over model complexity to handle the realities of data scarcity and interoperability in urban planning.

ABSTRACT

This article presents a GeoAI model designed to predict building vacancy in Ireland using only open and licensed-but-accessible datasets. It operates under mixed-access, proxy-based conditions, as legal and technical barriers frequently restrict access to proprietary data like utility consumption. Our model achieved a 0.379 F1-score and 0.348 F1-score under temporal holdout conditions, establishing a new baseline, with performance proving stronger in urban areas compared to rural regions. These results suggest limitations when relying solely on the available proxy data, highlighting the difficulty of detecting vacancy in environments where utility data are not readily available. This study prioritizes a schema-agnostic, reproducible architecture and governance framework over model complexity to handle the realities of data scarcity and interoperability in urban planning.

item.title: Sustainable Land Suitability Assessment for Garden City Development in Zanjan's Urban Hinterland Using Machine Learning
item.description: Transactions in GIS, Volume 30, Issue 7, November 2026.
item.dc:description: ABSTRACT In response to rapid urban expansion, population growth, and the need for sustainable land use, urban agriculture presents a viable strategy for enhancing food security and ecological balance in urban planning. This study aims to assess land suitability for garden city development in the urban hinterland zone of Zanjan. A hybrid framework integrating the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) with two machine learning (ML) methods, Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), was employed. A set of geospatial and environmental criteria, including slope, aspect, elevation, soil erosion, climatic variables (precipitation and temperature), and proximity to infrastructure and natural features, were analyzed to identify ecologically and socially suitable locations for garden city development. The standardized criteria were used as predictor variables, while expert‐informed suitability scores derived from the AHP framework served as reference values for model development. The results showed that the SVM and XGBoost models successfully learned the spatial suitability patterns represented by the expert‐informed AHP framework, achieving coefficients of determination of R2 = 0.988 and R2 = 0.977, respectively. These values indicate a high level of agreement between the ML predictions and the expert‐informed suitability patterns rather than independent predictive accuracy. The findings also revealed that distance from faults, access to urban infrastructure, and land slope were the most influential factors in determining suitable areas. The proposed hybrid framework demonstrates how expert knowledge and data‐driven learning can be integrated to support transparent and comprehensive land suitability assessment for garden city development in peri‐urban environments.

ABSTRACT

In response to rapid urban expansion, population growth, and the need for sustainable land use, urban agriculture presents a viable strategy for enhancing food security and ecological balance in urban planning. This study aims to assess land suitability for garden city development in the urban hinterland zone of Zanjan. A hybrid framework integrating the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) with two machine learning (ML) methods, Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), was employed. A set of geospatial and environmental criteria, including slope, aspect, elevation, soil erosion, climatic variables (precipitation and temperature), and proximity to infrastructure and natural features, were analyzed to identify ecologically and socially suitable locations for garden city development. The standardized criteria were used as predictor variables, while expert-informed suitability scores derived from the AHP framework served as reference values for model development. The results showed that the SVM and XGBoost models successfully learned the spatial suitability patterns represented by the expert-informed AHP framework, achieving coefficients of determination of R 2 = 0.988 and R 2 = 0.977, respectively. These values indicate a high level of agreement between the ML predictions and the expert-informed suitability patterns rather than independent predictive accuracy. The findings also revealed that distance from faults, access to urban infrastructure, and land slope were the most influential factors in determining suitable areas. The proposed hybrid framework demonstrates how expert knowledge and data-driven learning can be integrated to support transparent and comprehensive land suitability assessment for garden city development in peri-urban environments.
